findings.evidence: "'Vendor Onboarding' has been moved to archived projects. It no longer appears in the active projects list for anyone on the team." with only a single exit link, "Back to your projects" (#project-archived-exit-link), and no mention anywhere in the artifact of an archived-projects view or a restore/unarchive control.
findings.fix: Add a stated restore path: an archived-projects list reachable from the workspace overview, with an unarchive control, and link to it from the project-archived confirmation.
findings.violation: NNG-H3-UNDO requires a stated way back for an action that is reasonably reversible in the product being described; archiving a project is ordinarily reversible, but no restore or unarchive path appears anywhere in the eight states this artifact defines.

findings.evidence: The Save button (#invite-member-save-btn) submits the email form with no stated effect, while a separate Continue link (#invite-member-continue-link) is what actually leads to "Invite sent" (#invite-sent), whose copy reads "An invite was sent to the address entered above." On the project-settings and notification-settings screens, by contrast, the same "Save" label is the screen's one and only commit action.
findings.fix: Either make Save and Continue consistent with the other screens' single-commit pattern (drop one control), or relabel so the two controls' distinct roles are self-evident, e.g. rename Save to something that does not imply completion, such as "Check address".
findings.location: Invite a team member screen (#invite-member), the Save button versus Continue link
findings.violation: NNG-H4-INTERNAL requires that one label carry one meaning everywhere it appears; "Save" is the terminal, complete action on two screens but a non-terminal step preceding a separate commit (Continue) on this one, with no cue distinguishing the two meanings.

findings.evidence: "Import failed. Error code IMP-500. Contact support if this continues."
findings.fix: Replace or supplement the code with a plain-language cause, e.g. naming which file or step failed and why (format, size, permissions, connectivity).
findings.location: Import status screen (#import-status), the status message (#import-status-message)
findings.violation: NNG-H9-IDENTIFY requires error text specific enough that the user can tell which action or entry caused the failure; this message reports only that the import failed and surfaces a raw internal code, naming no file, field, or cause the user can act on.

findings.evidence: The only control on this screen is "Back to your projects" (#import-status-exit-link); the message's suggested step, "Contact support," has no link, address, or control anywhere on the screen or elsewhere in the artifact.
findings.fix: Add a retry control for the import and a working support contact (link, email, or in-app channel) directly on this screen.
findings.violation: NNG-H9-RECOVER requires that error text's suggested next step be reachable from where the message appears; this message suggests contacting support but gives no way to do so, and offers no retry control for the import itself, leaving the user's only path a return to the overview with the import still unresolved.

findings.evidence: <button id="project-settings-duplicate-btn" type="button" aria-label="Duplicate project"></button>: no href, no form, and no target state or message anywhere in the artifact names what happens after it is activated.
findings.fix: Define what Duplicate project does: either a result message on the same screen or a defined destination state (e.g. the new duplicate appearing in the project list), so the user can tell the action took effect.
findings.location: Project settings screen, the Duplicate project button (#project-settings-duplicate-btn)
findings.violation: NNG-H1 requires a visible indication of what the system is doing and what the outcome was for a state-changing action; this trigger is specified with no in-progress or result feedback at all, not even a destination state.

findings.evidence: <button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button> with no form action and no success or failure message defined anywhere in the project-settings section.
findings.fix: Specify a visible save confirmation (a message or a changed control state) that appears after Save is activated, on this screen and at each repeated instance.

instances.evidence: <button id="invite-member-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button> with no form action and no stated result.
instances.location: Invite a team member screen, the Save button (#invite-member-save-btn)

instances.evidence: <button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button> with no form action and no stated result.

findings.location: Project settings screen, the Save button (#project-settings-save-btn)
findings.violation: NNG-H1 requires that a state-changing action name what the user sees while it runs and once it finishes; the artifact names the Save trigger but specifies no in-progress or result feedback for it, on the same pattern repeated at two further instances.

findings.evidence: Cancel follows an email input the user has already filled in; nothing in the invite-member section or elsewhere states what becomes of that entered address.
findings.fix: State in place, next to Cancel, that the entered email address is discarded (or preserved) when Cancel is used.
findings.location: Invite a team member screen, the Cancel link (#invite-member-cancel-link)
findings.violation: NNG-H3-EXIT requires that an exit from a flow holding entered data states what happens to that data; the exit here is visible and clearly labeled, but its effect on the already-entered email address is unstated.

findings.evidence: "An invite was sent to the address entered above." is the entire content of this screen; the email address itself, entered on the previous invite-member screen, is not redisplayed here.
findings.fix: Redisplay the email address on the invite-sent confirmation itself, e.g. "An invite was sent to jane@example.com."
findings.violation: NNG-H6-RECALL requires that information the user needs at a step be present at that step rather than held over from an earlier screen; this confirmation refers to "the address entered above" on a screen where nothing is in fact above it, leaving the user to recall or re-verify an address they cannot currently see.
